Drywall & Ceiling Repair in Pleasanton, CA

Pleasanton spans more eras than almost any city in the Tri-Valley. Downtown around Main Street holds genuine Victorians and early-1900s homes; Vintage Hills and Val Vista are 1960s–80s tracts; Ruby Hill and the newer east side are large post-1990 customs.

Three eras, three different repairs. The build year is the first question we ask, because in downtown Pleasanton the answer is often "plaster".

What drywall work looks like in Pleasanton

The downtown historic district is the interesting part — small older homes with plaster over lath, original trim and low ceilings, where the right repair is conservative and the wrong one is a drywall square that cracks out. Vintage Hills, Birdland and Val Vista are conventional 1960s–80s tract stock with orange peel and predictable seam failure. Ruby Hill and the Foothill Road customs are big, tall and finished to a standard that punishes an approximate texture match.

Housing note: From 1890s downtown plaster to 2000s custom smooth-wall — confirm what is behind the paint before anyone quotes a patch.

Drywall questions from Pleasanton homeowners

Our downtown Pleasanton house is from 1905. Can you work on it? +

Yes. Expect plaster over lath, and expect us to repair it as plaster rather than cutting in a drywall patch that will crack around its edges within a year.

Do you travel to Pleasanton from the Walnut Creek side? +

Yes, it is inside our service area. Larger jobs are scheduled as full days there rather than short visits, which keeps the pricing sensible.

How much does drywall repair cost? +

It depends far more on access, height and texture than on the size of the hole. A single small patch at standard ceiling height is the least expensive job we do; the same patch on a two-storey entry wall costs several times more because of staging and protection. We give written quotes before any work starts.

Can you match my existing wall texture? +

Yes — orange peel, knockdown, skip trowel, hand-troweled and Level 5 smooth. For unusual or hand-applied finishes we prepare a sample panel and get your sign-off before touching the visible wall. Where a blend genuinely will not disappear, we will tell you that re-texturing the whole wall is the better answer rather than leaving you with a patch you can see.

Do you paint after the repair? +

We finish, texture and prime every repair so it is ready for paint and the sheen matches. Final colour coats are usually best handled by your painter, who has your exact paint — but ask, because on small jobs we can often finish it out.

How long does a typical repair take? +

Joint compound has to dry between coats, so most repairs are one long day or two shorter visits. Anyone promising a finished, textured, invisible repair in ninety minutes is skipping a coat.
